# Where the engine answers differently from upstream, found by replaying upstream's own tests (see
# internal/upstream). One divergence per line, TAB-separated:
#
#   <package> TAB <signature> TAB <reason citing upstream>
#
# Each replay asserts its lines exactly: a vector that diverges and is not listed fails, and a listed
# vector that now agrees fails too. A signature of `*ulp<=N` stands for every vector of the package that
# differs from upstream only by numbers within N units in the last place; the replay fails if none does.
#
# A package written <package>@<arch> lists divergences for vectors recorded on that architecture
# (node's process.arch) only; they are asserted the same way where they apply.
#
# An entry is added only when upstream is the one that is right and the fix is not small; the reason says
# which, and cites upstream.

d3-scale	scaleThreshold()().domain(["10","2"]).range([0,1,2])("12")	engine bug: Threshold bisects numerically (SetDomain coerces to numbers), where d3-scale threshold.js bisects the domain as given, so string thresholds compare lexicographically ("12" < "2" gives index 1, not 2). Numeric thresholds, the only kind a specification normally holds, agree.
vega-expression	parseExpression("[0,,]")	design: vega-expression's parser accepts an array elision and makes it a null element, but its code generator then throws on the null (Cannot read properties of null), so no expression with one ever compiles; the engine rejects it when parsing (internal/expr/parse.go parseArray), which is the same outcome for every use of an expression.
d3-geo@x64	geoCentroid({"coordinates":[[[[54.73561031724534,-29.999999999999993],[53.81999065308151,-28.832172942274624],[52.957795386825524,-27.639300153817125],[52.147578895325495,-26.42312865996355],[51.387893921962714,-25.18532227675056],[50.67731009036001,-23.927464720758973],[50.014429245419485,-22.65106…	platform: the same fused multiply-add difference as d3-ease@x64, in the sin and cos the centroid and circle sum; the answers are rounding noise around zero (or a whole degree) that the two builds of V8 round differently. jsmath with the fusions removed gives x64's answer.
d3-geo@x64	geoCentroid({"$origin":{"chain":[["radius",[5]],["center",[[30,45]]]],"constructedWith":[],"from":"geoCircle()","steps":[[null,[]]]},"coordinates":[[[23.025992350148787,44.35041479262567],[22.988126590018105,44.522607784018554],[22.95848019814789,44.695627966327514],[22.93716127350285,44.86927260070…	platform: the same fused multiply-add difference as d3-ease@x64, in the sin and cos the centroid and circle sum; the answers are rounding noise around zero (or a whole degree) that the two builds of V8 round differently. jsmath with the fusions removed gives x64's answer.
d3-geo@x64	geoCentroid({"coordinates":[[[-26.10013878228641,-10.182067403158893],[-27.733647486630456,-9.541845517682908],[-29.349243068091596,-8.866131929297728],[-30.946539024794003,-8.155856375183232],[-32.525242557030815,-7.411964470431642],[-34.08515166400732,-6.635413291894852],[-35.62615174821801,-5.827…	platform: the same fused multiply-add difference as d3-ease@x64, in the sin and cos the centroid and circle sum; the answers are rounding noise around zero (or a whole degree) that the two builds of V8 round differently. jsmath with the fusions removed gives x64's answer.
d3-geo@x64	geoCircle()().center([0,90])()	platform: the same fused multiply-add difference as d3-ease@x64, in the sin and cos the centroid and circle sum; the answers are rounding noise around zero (or a whole degree) that the two builds of V8 round differently. jsmath with the fusions removed gives x64's answer.
d3-ease@x64	easeSinOut(0.3)	platform: easeSinOut is Math.sin(t * halfPi); jsmath follows V8's fdlibm as clang builds it for arm64, contracting a*b+c into fused multiply-adds, and clang does not contract on x64, so V8 there rounds sin(0.4712388980384690) to 0.45399049973954675 where the engine (and node on arm64) gives 0.4539904997395468. jsmath with the fusions removed gives x64's answer.
d3-geo@x64	*ulp<=8	platform: the same fused multiply-add difference as d3-ease@x64, in the trigonometric functions geoCircle computes its ring with: the points differ from upstream by a few units in the last place because jsmath fuses where V8 on x64 does not. jsmath with the fusions removed gives x64's answer.
vega-statistics@x64	*ulp<=8	platform: the same fused multiply-add difference as d3-ease@x64, in the Math.log of randomNormal (and of randomKDE, which samples it): the samples differ from upstream by a few units in the last place because jsmath fuses where V8 on x64 does not. jsmath with the fusions removed gives x64's answer.
